title: Entra ID Conditional Access Blocked Sign-Ins

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:signinlog` events with `status.errorCode!="0"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.25 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:signinlog` traffic without `status.errorCode!="0"`. Confirm UC-4.2.25 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:signinlog` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:signinlog" status.errorCode!="0"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.25_entra_id_conditional_acc_25"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.25 — Entra ID Conditional Access Blocked Sign-Ins: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:signinlog` for search criteria `status.errorCode!="0"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Entra ID Conditional Access Blocked Sign-Ins' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.25 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Forward sign-in logs. Filter for resultType or status indicating block (e.g. conditional access block). Alert on spike in blocks or blocks for sensitive apps. Correlate with risk and device compliance.
visualization: Table (user, app, error, location), Bar chart (blocks by reason), Timeline.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
  by Authentication.user Authentication.action Authentication.src span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Authentication (Authentication dataset).
knownFalsePositives: Some risky scores come from new devices, working from home, or a partner logging in the same way we do. We do not want every medium flag to page us; we pair higher scores with new locations, odd hours, or multiple clouds before we act.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:signinlog`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Forward sign-in logs. Filter for resultType or status indicating block (e.g. conditional access block). Alert on spike in blocks or blocks for sensitive apps. Correlate with risk and device compliance.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:signinlog" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:signinlog" status.errorCode!="0"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.25_entra_id_conditional_acc_25"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:signinlog` in `index=azure` to detect entra id conditional access blocked sign-ins. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_25_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (user, app, error, location), Bar chart (blocks by reason), Timeline..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of entra id conditional access blocked sign-ins so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
